prospect.name: Daniel
prospect.location: Rochester, Minnesota, USA; originally from Ecuador and living alone in the US
prospect.occupation: Working a new job while studying radiology; recently medically discharged from the military and currently completing orientation at the new job
prospect.family_status: Married — introduced his wife, her sister and her nephew to the gym; lives alone in the US with family visiting from abroad
prospect.training_background: Training in gyms since high school and describes exercise as a hobby. Previously worked with personal trainers in Ecuador who were powerlifters and bodybuilders; declined their approach because he wants to stay natural. Has done military boot camps and dislikes running and CrossFit-style work. Started kettlebells about a month ago after seeing Trevor's videos, alongside his regular gym training and cardio. Tracks his calories at 2,300-2,700 a day and has taken body fat from 25% to about 20%.
prospect.medical: Herniated disc for many years with chronic pain that materially affects daily life — 'even on long drives and sitting down for long periods of time or laying down for long periods of time is kind of painful. So even if I want to study, I have to stand up all the time.' Sleep limited to about five hours historically because of it. Under medical care: 'I went to the doctor and they did a myofascial release on my lower back muscles.' Reports that one month of kettlebell work has already reduced the pain. Also recently received a medical discharge from the military; the reason was not asked. Reports abdominal 'inflammation' he associates with a previous powerlifting bulk.

signals: Lost ground to a hard season on several fronts at once — a military medical discharge, falling behind on a mortgage and HOA to the tune of $13,000-$14,000, and years of chronic back pain
Wants a capability he feels he has never had rather than pure aesthetics: 'I've never had that, like, a strong core... one of the main objectives, gain some muscle on my lower back'
Motivation is escape from a deteriorating baseline: 'living with pain is not life' and 'if I don't work out, I know there'll be a point where I can't even stand up'

Counter-signals kept confidence at 0.65: he has trained continuously since high school and is training now, so he has not physically detrained, and the decisive blocker was money rather than the body. He is not the_medically_constrained either, because no clinician has ruled the programme out — nobody asked one.

goals.text: Get visible abs, which he has wanted since high school
Build a strong core and muscle around his lower back to stabilise the herniated disc
Live without back pain — 'living with pain is not life'
Learn correct kettlebell technique so he does not injure himself
Get leaner from around 20-23% body fat
Have a structured routine rather than improvising sessions
Build an athletic, functional physique rather than a bodybuilder look, and stay natural
Be able to sit, drive and study without pain, and sleep more than five hours

pains.text: Herniated disc with chronic pain that limits sitting, driving, lying down and studying — 'I used to never receive classes sitting down because I would feel so much pain'
Sleep restricted to about five hours by the pain
Fear that stopping training leads to total loss of function — 'if I don't work out, I know there'll be a point where I can't even stand up'
No confidence in his kettlebell technique after one month — 'it's the first time I ever do these type of exercises'
Severe financial pressure: cleared $13,000-$14,000 of mortgage and HOA arrears accumulated during military service, currently taking a loan to pay a university semester, roughly $100 a month spare
Recent medical discharge from the military and a new job with no overtime available yet
Never enjoyed the training modalities he has been exposed to — running, abs work, CrossFit, bodybuilding-style coaching
Body fat drifted from 20% to 23% during a month of family visits and eating out

objections.raw_quote: Well, I definitely don't have that. At the moment, but I would have to, like, text back or something.
objections.rep_response: Isolated it immediately ('outside of the investment, do you feel like, yes, I want to get started?'), pushed for a 1-10 rating of the programme with money set aside, ran the worth test, then took the full financial picture — cash available, monthly surplus, credit score — and floated $500 a month over twelve months.

objections.raw_quote: Well, I'm just a little surprised of the price, $6,000. So it's like $1,000 per month.
objections.rep_response: Set money aside and asked him to score the programme itself out of ten, which produced a strong endorsement of the offer independent of price.

objections.raw_quote: I recently got back from the military, and I got a medical discharge, and throughout the whole time I was in the military, I fell behind on my mortgage, I fell behind on my HOA, so I had to pay like over $10,000... And I would say this year, I see it impossible. I would say next year.
objections.rep_response: Accepted it without running any urgency play, praised the honesty, told him the cheap tier would not give him the form correction he needs, and closed to staying in contact and starting next year.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Rep floated splitting the $6,000 across twelve months at $500 per month: 'when do you feel like you would be able to go for like 500 a month, if we split it up over 12 months?' No terms, provider or interest were discussed and the prospect could not meet it.

evidence: Explicit and unambiguous on capacity: 'I mean, to be honest, nothing close to that' and 'this year, I see it impossible. I would say next year.'
Monthly ceiling of about $100 against a $6,000 price and a $500/month proposed plan
The rep closed it out himself: 'we'll just stay in contact and get you started when it's a better time'
No payment, no link, no next call, no date — only a video to be sent on WhatsApp

Counter-evidence on intent, which is unusually strong: he rated the programme highly with money set aside, confirmed 'do you feel like that is worth $6,000 to you? Definitely. Definitely', and said 'if it wasn't for the investment right now, I would totally be interested in joining the program'. This is a lost deal on capacity alone, not on desire or belief.
outcome.next_step: Rep to send a video on WhatsApp; open-ended contact, with a view to revisiting next year.

notable.note: Two opposite things sit in the same call. Clinically it is the most exposed in the batch after Pete: a prospect with a years-old herniated disc, pain severe enough to prevent him sitting through classes and sleeping more than five hours, currently under a doctor's care for it, and recently medically discharged from the military — and the rep sold a $6,000 loaded kettlebell programme with the explicit promise that the disc pain would reduce, without ever asking whether a clinician had cleared him or what the discharge was for. Commercially, though, this is the most disciplined money conversation in the batch: the rep ran the financial picture properly, did not discount, and — uniquely in this folder — actively declined to downsell, telling the prospect that the cheap tier 'is also not where you're going to actually get the form that you would need'. The blemish is that he asked for a credit score and floated $500 a month immediately after the prospect disclosed he was taking a loan to pay tuition and had $100 spare.
